'''David Arthur Eppstein''' (born 1963) is an American [[computer scientist]] and mathematician. He is a distinguished professor of [[computer science]] at the [[University of California, Irvine]],<ref name=photographer/><ref>{{cite web|title=Distinguished Professors – UCI|url=https://ap.uci.edu/titles-of-distinction/distinguished-professor/|access-date=July 26, 2020|archive-date=September 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200916202917/https://ap.uci.edu/titles-of-distinction/distinguished-professor/|url-status=live}}</ref> known for his work in [[computational geometry]], [[Graph theory|graph algorithms]], and [[recreational mathematics]]. Eppstein is also a [[Wikipedia]] editor and an administrator on the [[English Wikipedia]].

==Education and career==
Eppstein received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in [[mathematics]] from [[Stanford University]] in 1984, and later an [[Master of Science|M.S.]] (1985) and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] (1989) in computer science from [[Columbia University]], after which he took a postdoctoral position at [[Xerox]]'s [[Palo Alto Research Center]].<ref>{{cite journal |date=September 2000 |title=Contributors |journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory |volume=47 |issue=6 |pages=2667–2677 |doi=10.1109/TIT.2001.945287 }}</ref> He joined the UC Irvine faculty in 1990, and was co-chair of the Computer Science Department there from 2002 to 2005.<ref name="Vitae">{{cite web|title=David Eppstein's Online Curriculum Vitae|url=https://www.ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/vita.pdf|access-date=April 9, 2008|archive-date=January 27, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120127234710/http://www.ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/vita.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2014, he was named a Chancellor's Professor.<ref>{{cite web|title=UCI Chancellor's Professors|url=http://www.ap.uci.edu/distinctions/chancprof.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021115173118/http://www.ap.uci.edu/distinctions/chancprof.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 15, 2002|access-date=August 18, 2014|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

He obtained his Ph.D. in computer science in 1989, from Columbia University, advised by [[Zvi Galil]]. He has supervised thirteen PhD. students, all at University of California, Irvine.<ref>{{cite web | title=David Eppstein - the Mathematics Genealogy Project | url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=120697 }}</ref>

Eppstein was named an [[ACM Fellow]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://awards.acm.org/fellows/award-winners|title=List of ACM Fellows|access-date=September 9, 2019|archive-date=December 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161201132101/http://awards.acm.org/fellow/all.cfm|url-status=live}}</ref> In October 2017, he was one of 396 members elected as fellows of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=American Association for the Advancement of Science|title=2017 AAAS Fellows approved by the AAAS Council|journal=Science|volume=358|issue=6366|pages=1011–1014|doi=10.1126/science.358.6366.1011|year=2017|bibcode=2017Sci...358.1011.|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Eppstein is an amateur [[digital photographer]].<ref name=photographer>{{cite news|author=Hines, Michael|title=Picture-perfect prints are possible|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/238407757|access-date=September 9, 2019|work=[[Daily Press (Virginia)|Daily Press]]|date=September 1, 2001|location=Hampton, VA|page=G1, G7|department=Business|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|url-access=limited|quote=Eppstein is a computer science professor at the University of California, Irvine, and member of the rec.photo.digital online bulletin board of amateur digital photographers.|archive-date=June 14, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190614155516/http://www.newspapers.com/image/238407757/|url-status=live}}</ref> He is also a [[Wikipedia]] editor and tries to bring more experts to the project.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Eppstein | first1=David | last2=Lewis | first2=Joel Brewster | last3=Woodroofe | first3=Russ | title={Princ-wiki-a Mathematica}: Wikipedia Editing and Mathematics | journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume=72 | issue=1 | date=2025 | issn=0002-9920 | doi=10.1090/noti3096  | doi-access=free| page=1| arxiv=2412.20419 }}</ref>

Eppstein served as the program chair for the theory track of the ACM [[Symposium on Computational Geometry]] in 2001<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACM Symposium on Computional Geometry 2001: Conference Program |url=https://sarielhp.org/research/CG/compgeom/msg00389.html |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=sarielhp.org}}</ref>, the program chair of the ACM-SIAM [[Symposium on Discrete Algorithms]] in 2002<ref>{{Cite web |title=About the Symposium |url=https://www.siam.org/meetings/da02/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060210013944/https://www.siam.org/meetings/da02/ |archive-date=2006-02-10 |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=www.siam.org}}</ref>, and the co-chair for the [[International Symposium on Graph Drawing]] in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Call For Papers: Graph Drawing 2009 |url=http://facweb.cs.depaul.edu/gd2009/cfp.asp#pc |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=facweb.cs.depaul.edu |archive-date=2025-10-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007233447/http://facweb.cs.depaul.edu/gd2009/cfp.asp#pc |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Research interests==
In computer science, Eppstein's research has included work on [[minimum spanning tree]]s, [[shortest path]]s, dynamic [[graph data structure]]s, [[graph coloring]], [[graph drawing]] and [[geometric]] [[Optimization (mathematics)|optimization]]. He has published also in application areas such as [[finite element meshing]], which is used in engineering design, and in [[computational statistics]], particularly in [[robust statistics|robust]], [[multivariate statistics|multivariate]], [[nonparametric statistics]].
